title_en: Rules on Supervision of Administrative Proceedings by People's Procuratorates

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Rules are formulated in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Organic Law of the People's Procuratorates of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant provisions, and in light of the actual work of the People's Procuratorates, for the purpose of ensuring and regulating the People's Procuratorates' performance of their duties of supervision over administrative litigation according to law.

Article 2 The People's Procuratorates shall independently exercise the procuratorial power according to law, and through handling cases of supervision over administrative litigation, shall supervise the People's Courts in adjudication and enforcement according to law, promote administrative organs in exercising their powers according to law, maintain judicial fairness and judicial authority, safeguard national interests and social public interests, protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, promote substantive resolution of administrative disputes, and ensure the uniform and correct implementation of national laws.
Article 3 The People's Procuratorates shall exercise legal supervision over administrative litigation by means of filing protests, issuing procuratorial recommendations, and other means.

Article 4 In exercising legal supervision over administrative litigation, the People's Procuratorates shall take facts as the basis and law as the criterion, adhere to openness, fairness, and justice, conduct comprehensive review according to law, and supervise and support the People's Courts and administrative organs in exercising their powers according to law.

Article 5 A People's Procuratorate, when handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, shall adopt a procedure for separating complex cases from simple ones, handling complex cases carefully and simple cases quickly.
When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, a People's Procuratorate shall strengthen the use of intelligence and assistance; for major, difficult, and complex issues, it may consult experts or organize expert deliberation to hear expert opinions and suggestions.

Article 6 When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, the People's Procuratorate shall ascertain the facts of the case and distinguish right from wrong, and comprehensively use means such as supervision and correction, public hearings, legal interpretation and reasoning, and judicial assistance to carry out the work of substantive resolution of administrative disputes.

Article 7 The departments responsible for complaint and petition prosecution, administrative prosecution, and case management shall respectively undertake the acceptance, handling, and management of cases of supervision over administrative litigation, and all departments shall cooperate with and constrain each other.
Cases where a party refuses to accept an effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement on administrative compensation made by the People's Court shall be handled by the department responsible for administrative prosecution, and the provisions of these Rules shall apply.

Article 8 When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, the People's Procuratorate shall have the prosecutor, the Chief Prosecutor, and the Procuratorial Committee make decisions on case-handling matters within their respective scope of functions and assume corresponding judicial responsibility according to the provisions.
A prosecutor shall carry out work under the leadership of the Chief Prosecutor. Major case-handling matters shall be decided by the Chief Prosecutor. The Chief Prosecutor may, based on the circumstances of the case, submit them to the Procuratorial Committee for discussion and decision. Other case-handling matters may be decided by the Chief Prosecutor personally, or the Chief Prosecutor may delegate them to a prosecutor for decision.
Where these Rules have explicit provisions on major case-handling matters that shall be decided by the Chief Prosecutor or the Procuratorial Committee, such provisions shall be followed; where these Rules do not have explicit provisions, the people's procuratorate of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may formulate relevant provisions, subject to the approval of the Supreme People's Procuratorate.
Legal documents issued in the name of a People's Procuratorate shall be signed and issued by the Chief Prosecutor; for matters falling within the decision-making authority of a prosecutor, the Chief Prosecutor may authorize the prosecutor to sign and issue them.
For cases that are major, difficult, complex, or have social impact, a report shall be made to the Chief Prosecutor.

Article 9 When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, a People's Procuratorate may, based on the circumstances of the case, have a single prosecutor handle the case alone, or form a case-handling group composed of two or more prosecutors. Where a case is handled by a prosecutor case-handling group, the Chief Prosecutor shall designate one prosecutor as the lead prosecutor to organize and direct the case-handling group in handling the case.
When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, a prosecutor may, as needed, be assisted by prosecutorial auxiliary personnel such as prosecutor assistants, clerks, judicial police, and prosecutorial technicians. Such prosecutorial auxiliary personnel shall undertake corresponding prosecutorial auxiliary matters in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 10 The Supreme People's Procuratorate shall lead the supervision over administrative litigation carried out by local People's Procuratorates at all levels and by special People's Procuratorates, and a People's Procuratorate at a higher level shall lead the supervision over administrative litigation carried out by a People's Procuratorate at a lower level.
Where a People's Procuratorate at a higher level considers that a decision made by a People's Procuratorate at a lower level is erroneous, it has the authority to instruct the lower-level People's Procuratorate to correct it, or to revoke or change it according to law. A decision made by a People's Procuratorate at a higher level shall be made in writing, and the lower-level People's Procuratorate shall implement it. If a lower-level People's Procuratorate disagrees with the decision of the higher-level People's Procuratorate, it may report to the higher-level People's Procuratorate while implementing it.
A People's Procuratorate at a higher level may, according to law, uniformly deploy prosecutorial personnel within its jurisdiction to handle cases of supervision over administrative litigation; the decision on deployment shall be made in writing. The deployed prosecutor may represent the handling People's Procuratorate in performing relevant prosecutorial duties.

Article 11 When the trial committee of a People's Court at the same level discusses a case of supervision over administrative litigation or other topics related to the work of supervision over administrative litigation, the Chief Prosecutor of the People's Procuratorate or a deputy Chief Prosecutor authorized by the Chief Prosecutor may attend the meeting as a non-voting participant in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 12 When handling a case of supervision over administrative litigation, prosecutorial personnel shall uphold an objective and impartial stance and consciously subject themselves to supervision.
Prosecutorial personnel shall not have contacts or dealings with parties, lawyers, persons with special relationships, or intermediary organizations in violation of regulations.
Where prosecutorial personnel engage in acts such as accepting bribes or bending the law for personal gain, they shall be subject to disciplinary liability and legal liability.
Prosecutorial personnel shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, comprehensively, truthfully, and promptly record and report on actions such as inquiries about or interference in the handling of cases of supervision over administrative litigation, which constitute material matters.
Article 14 Where prosecutorial personnel voluntarily withdraw, they may do so orally or in writing, stating the reasons. An oral application shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 15 A party applying for withdrawal shall do so orally or in writing before the People's Procuratorate makes a decision on filing a protest or issuing a procuratorial recommendation or other decisions, and shall state the reasons. An oral application shall be recorded in the case file. Where an application for withdrawal is made pursuant to the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 13 of these Rules, relevant evidence shall be provided.
The person subject to a withdrawal application shall suspend work on the case until the People's Procuratorate makes a decision on whether to withdraw, except where emergency measures are required for the case.

Article 16 The withdrawal of the Chief Prosecutor shall be discussed and decided by the Procuratorial Committee; the withdrawal of prosecutorial personnel and other personnel shall be decided by the Chief Prosecutor. When the Procuratorial Committee discusses the withdrawal of the Chief Prosecutor, the meeting shall be presided over by a deputy Chief Prosecutor, and the Chief Prosecutor shall not participate.

Article 17 A People's Procuratorate shall make a decision on a party's application for withdrawal within three days and notify the applicant. An application that is clearly not based on statutory grounds for withdrawal may be rejected on the spot and recorded in the case file.
If the applicant is dissatisfied with the decision rejecting the application for withdrawal, they may, at the time of receiving the decision, apply to the original decision-making body for reconsideration once. The People's Procuratorate shall make a reconsideration decision within three days and notify the reconsideration applicant. During the reconsideration period, the person subject to the withdrawal application shall not cease work on the case.

Article 21 A party applying to the People's Procuratorate for supervision shall submit an application for supervision, identity certificate, relevant legal documents, and evidentiary materials. Where evidentiary materials are submitted, a list of evidence shall be attached.
If the application materials for supervision are incomplete, the People's Procuratorate shall require the applicant to complete them within a specified time limit, and shall inform the applicant at one time of all the materials to be completed and the legal consequences of failing to complete them as required within the time limit, which shall be deemed as withdrawal of the supervision application. If the applicant fails to complete the main materials within the time limit, it shall be deemed as withdrawal of the supervision application.

Article 23 The identity certificate as provided in Article 21 of these Rules includes:
(1) for citizens, their resident identity card, military officer card, soldier card, passport, or other valid documents capable of proving their identity;
(2) for legal persons or other organizations, their unified social credit code certificate or business license, identity certificate of their legal representative or principal responsible person, or other valid certificates.
The People's Procuratorate shall, after verifying that the identity certificate submitted by a party is correct, retain a photocopy.

Article 24 The relevant legal documents as provided in Article 21 of these Rules refer to all judgments, rulings, decisions, mediation documents, and other legal documents made by the People's Court in the litigation process of the case.
Article 25 A party applying for supervision may, in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, appoint an authorized agent.

Article 28 Where a party applies to the People's Procuratorate for supervision regarding an administrative judgment, ruling, or mediation document that has become legally effective, the case shall be accepted by the department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that made the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document.

Article 29 Where a party believes that a judge has committed an illegal act in the administrative adjudication procedure or that there is an illegal circumstance in an enforcement activity, and applies to the People's Procuratorate for supervision, the case shall be accepted by the department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that tried or enforced the case.
Where a party refuses to accept a reconsideration ruling, decision, or the like made by the People's Court superior to the People's Court that tried or enforced the case, and applies to the People's Procuratorate for supervision, the case shall be accepted by the department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that made the reconsideration ruling, decision, or the like.

Article 30 Where the People's Procuratorate fails to accept a party's supervision application according to law, the party may apply for supervision to the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level. If the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level deems that the party's supervision application meets the acceptance conditions, it shall instruct the People's Procuratorate at the next lower level to accept the case; where necessary, it may directly accept the case.

Article 32 The department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work shall, within three days from the date of deciding to accept the case, prepare a Notice of Acceptance, serve it on the applicant, and inform the applicant of his or her rights and obligations.
Where other parties need to be notified, it shall serve the Notice of Acceptance and a copy of the supervision application on such other parties and inform them of their rights and obligations. Other parties may submit written opinions within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the copy of the supervision application; failure to submit opinions shall not affect the People's Procuratorate's review of the case.

Article 33 The department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work shall, within three days from the date of deciding to accept the case, transfer the case materials to the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work of this People's Procuratorate, and at the same time send a copy of the Notice of Acceptance to the department responsible for case management of this People's Procuratorate. Where the department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work receives materials such as written opinions submitted by other parties, it shall promptly transfer them to the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work.

Article 34 Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations other than the parties who believe that a judge has committed an illegal act in the administrative adjudication procedure of the People's Court or that there is an illegal circumstance in an enforcement activity may file a complaint with the People's Procuratorate at the same level. The complaint shall be accepted by the department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate.
The department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work shall handle the received complaint in accordance with the Provisions on the Work of Letters and Visits of the People's Procuratorate and other relevant regulations.

Article 35 The department responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work may, in accordance with the Provisions on the Work of Letters and Visits of the People's Procuratorate, assign to the People's Procuratorate at a lower level the handling of letter and visit cases involving supervision of administrative proceedings.

Article 37 Cases where the People's Procuratorate at a lower level submits a request for protest or for other supervision shall be accepted by the department responsible for case management of the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level.
For cases subject to supervision ex officio, the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work shall register the acceptance with the department responsible for case management.

Article 38 After receiving the case materials, the department responsible for case management shall, within three days, register the case and transfer the case materials and the case registration form to the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work; if the case materials do not conform to the requirements, it shall require them to be completed.
After the department responsible for case management registers the acceptance, if it is necessary to notify the parties, the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work shall prepare a Notice of Acceptance and serve it on the parties within three days.

Article 105 Where the People's Procuratorate discovers that a judicial officer in the administrative adjudication proceedings of a people's court at the same level has committed illegal acts as specified in Article 46 of the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China or other provisions, which may affect the fair adjudication or enforcement of the case, it shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the people's court at the same level.

Article 106 When a People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation in accordance with this Chapter, it shall obtain approval from the Chief Procurator or a decision by the Procuratorial Committee, prepare a "Procuratorial Recommendation Letter", and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, transfer the "Procuratorial Recommendation Letter" together with the case file to the people's court at the same level. For a case where a party applies for supervision, the People's Procuratorate shall prepare a notice document and send it to the applicant.

Article 107 Where the People's Procuratorate considers that the basis for determining the illegal acts of the judicial officer in the administrative adjudication proceedings for which a party has applied for supervision is insufficient, it shall make a decision not to support the application for supervision, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, prepare a "Decision Letter Not to Support the Supervision Application", and send it to the applicant.
Article 108 The People's Procuratorate shall exercise legal supervision over the enforcement activities of people's courts in administrative cases.

Article 110 Where the People's Procuratorate discovers that a people's court, in the course of enforcement activities, has taken enforcement implementation measures such as investigation, sealing up, distraining, freezing, appraisal, auction, sale, custody, return of property, and credit punishment in violation of regulations, it shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the people's court at the same level.

Article 112 Where the People's Procuratorate considers that a people's court may have a situation of neglecting to perform its duties in the enforcement activities of an administrative case, it may issue a "Notice to Explain the Case Enforcement Situation" to the people's court, requesting an explanation of the enforcement situation and reasons of the case, and a written reply to the People's Procuratorate within fifteen days.
Article 113 Where a People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation in accordance with this Chapter, the provisions of Article 106 of these Rules shall apply.

Article 114 For an enforcement supervision case applied for by a party, if the People's Procuratorate considers that there is no illegal circumstance in the enforcement activities of the people's court, it shall make a decision not to support the supervision application, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, prepare a "Decision Letter Not to Support the Supervision Application", and send it to the applicant.

Article 115 Where the People's Procuratorate discovers that an enforcement officer has committed an illegal act in the enforcement activities of an administrative case of a people's court at the same level, it shall be handled by reference to the relevant provisions of Chapter VI of these Rules.

Article 116 The case management department of the People's Procuratorate shall manage, supervise, and give early warning on the acceptance, time limits, procedures, quality, etc. of administrative litigation supervision cases.

Article 117 The case management department shall exercise supervisory management over the preparation and issuance of legal documents for administrative litigation supervision in the name of the People's Procuratorate.

Article 120 Where the People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation for improving work and perfecting governance in accordance with relevant provisions, it shall prepare and issue one procuratorial recommendation for similar illegal circumstances.
Article 122 The People's Procuratorate may organize and carry out special supervision activities targeting common or prominent issues in administrative litigation supervision.

Article 123 Where the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate, in the course of performing its duties, discovers conduct suspected of violating discipline, committing crimes, or subject to the investigation of judicial responsibility, it shall, upon approval by the Chief Procurator, promptly transfer the relevant leads and materials to the organ or department with jurisdiction.
Where other functional departments of the People's Procuratorate, in the course of performing their duties, discover leads of administrative litigation supervision cases that shall be supervised ex officio in accordance with these Rules, they shall promptly notify the department responsible for administrative procuratorial work.

Article 124 After a people's court renders a retrial judgment, ruling, or other handling decision on an administrative litigation supervision case, the People's Procuratorate that issued the supervision opinion shall review the handling result and fill out the "Registration Form for Review of Handling Results of Administrative Litigation Supervision Cases".

Article 126 Local People's Procuratorates at all levels may request instructions from the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level for major administrative litigation supervision cases where the application of law is indeed difficult and complex and the procuratorate itself finds it hard to decide.
Cases requesting instructions shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on handling requests for instructions from lower-level People's Procuratorates and on the submission of official documents by lower-level People's Procuratorates to the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 127 Where the People's Procuratorate discovers that a relevant decision it has made is indeed erroneous or there are other circumstances requiring withdrawal or modification, the matter shall be subject to approval by the Chief Procurator or a decision by the Procuratorial Committee.

Article 128 Where the People's Court raises a written objection to the supervision act of the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall reply in writing to the People's Court with the result of its handling within the prescribed time limit. Where the People's Court still has objections to the reply and raises them through the People's Court at the next higher level to the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level, and the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level considers the objection of the People's Court to be correct, it shall require the lower-level People's Procuratorate to make timely corrections.

Article 129 The production of legal documents for administrative litigation supervision shall conform to the prescribed format.
The format of legal documents for administrative litigation supervision shall be formulated separately.

Article 130 The People's Procuratorate may serve legal documents by reference to the relevant provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Article 131 Where the People's Procuratorate discovers a clerical error in the legal document it has produced, it shall make a "Decision on Correction" to rectify the error.
Article 132 When handling administrative litigation supervision cases, the People's Procuratorate shall open files and archive them in accordance with the provisions.

Article 133 When handling administrative litigation supervision cases, the People's Procuratorate shall not charge any case acceptance fee. The fees incurred from applications for copying, expert evaluation, audit, inspection, etc. shall be paid directly by the applicant to the relevant institution or unit, and the People's Procuratorate shall not collect or pay on behalf of the applicant.

Article 134 When handling administrative litigation supervision cases, the People's Procuratorate may grant judicial assistance according to law where the applicant's claim has a certain degree of reasonableness but is difficult to resolve through legal channels and the applicant is in financial difficulty.
For applicants who are not covered by the scope of national judicial assistance or who still face financial difficulty after receiving national judicial assistance, they may be guided to apply for social assistance in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 135 Where these Rules do not provide for matters concerning the handling of administrative litigation supervision cases by the People's Procuratorate, the relevant provisions of the Rules of the People's Procuratorate for Civil Litigation Supervision shall apply.

Article 136 Where the People's Procuratorate, when handling administrative litigation supervision cases, issues procuratorial suggestions to relevant entities and departments, and these Rules do not provide for the relevant matters, the provisions of the Provisions of the People's Procuratorate on Procuratorial Suggestions Work shall apply.

Article 137 These Rules shall come into force as of September 1, 2021, and the Rules of the People's Procuratorate for Administrative Litigation Supervision (for Trial Implementation) shall be abolished simultaneously. Where other provisions previously promulgated by this Procuratorate are inconsistent with these Rules, these Rules shall prevail.
Supreme People's Procuratorate
Procuratorial Interpretation No. 3 [2021] of the Supreme People's Procuratorate
